newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat drops as Egypt buys French wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat drops as Egypt buys French wheat.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures fell early on news Egypt over the weekend bought 450,000 tonnes of wheat from France, traders said.
"The (export) competition continues with Egypt now going to France instead of us," a trader said.
Soybeans and corn were lower on a National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for above normal temperatures in the U.S. Midwest from September 19 through September 23.
Technical selling was noted as November soy overnight broke support at $8.00 per bushel and December corn fell below support at $3.20 per bushel, they said.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report showed non-commercials as of September 10 were long soybeans by roughly 9.7 to 1.0, long corn about 2.2 to 1.0 and short wheat by about 1.3 to 1.0.
The market shrugged off news of light frost over the weekend in portions of southern Minnesota and northern Iowa.
Agronomists said frost early Saturday damaged corn and soybeans in some low-lying fields in northern Iowa and southern Minnesota.
Markets remain volatile and meteorlogists early Monday said Midwest weather patterns are expected to remain volatile.
At 0955 CDT, wheat was three to eight cents per bushel lower, with September down seven at $4.22 and December down 6-1/2 at $4.17-1/2.

Soybeans were 3-1/2 to 10 cents per bushel lower, with September down nine at $8.19-1/2 and November down nine at $7.93. Soyoil was 0.21 to 0.27 cent per lb lower and soymeal was $2.70 to $3.30 per ton lower.
Corn was two to four cents per bushel lower, with September down 2-1/4 at $3.59-1/2 and December was down 3-1/2 at $3.18.
